$comment: The axe run options every Airness accessibility scan adds to axe's defaults: the browser sweep and scopedAxe of @airness/node, and AxeAudit of airness-web-evidence, which packages this file as a classpath resource. It is the one definition of the rule set, so a crawled page and a page a Java test audits cannot be asked different questions. Rules are turned on by id under rules, which adds to axe's default set; a runOnly tag list would replace that set and drop every best-practice rule. The rules every project is held to: identical-links-same-purpose (2.4.9), meta-refresh-no-exceptions (2.2.4 and 3.2.5, no timed refresh at any delay), target-size (2.5.8: 24 CSS pixels, or the room of a 24 pixel circle around a smaller target), and the experimental css-orientation-lock (1.3.4), p-as-heading, td-has-header and table-fake-caption (1.3.1); axe's default color-contrast (1.4.3, 4.5:1) runs beside them. The experimental hidden-content and focus-order-semantics stay off, because they report only items to look at by eye. Under levels, each of the two rules whose AAA level costs a design the most adds what a project that raises it to AAA is held to: contrast turns on color-contrast-enhanced (1.4.6, 7:1), and targetSize measures a target at the 44 CSS pixels of 2.5.5 with the target-offset check off, because it passes an undersized target for the room around it, the spacing exception of 2.5.8, which 2.5.5 does not grant. A target within a line of text stays exempt at either level, because the rule never selects one.
